sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Energy Flow**: Follows the **10% Law (Lindeman)**, where only 10% of energy is transferred to the next trophic level, limiting food chain length.
• **Nutrient Cycling**: Biogeochemical cycles (Carbon, Nitrogen, Phosphorus) ensure the **conservation of matter** within the biosphere.
• **Succession**: The directional, predictable change in species composition over time, culminating in a **Climax Community**.
• **Homeostasis**: The ability of an ecosystem to maintain internal stability through **negative feedback loops** despite external disturbances.

The percentage of energy transferred from one trophic level to the next; typically ranges from 5% to 20%.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Ecosystem Services**: Provisioning, regulating, cultural, and supporting services defined by the Millennium Ecosystem Assessment.
• **Ecological Restoration**: Active intervention (e.g., CAMPA funds) to accelerate recovery of degraded ecosystems.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Habitat fragmentation, invasive species, and climate-induced phenological mismatch.
• **Solutions**: Nature-based Solutions (NbS) and landscape-level conservation approaches.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-S-C' (Pioneer, Seral, Climax).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P (Pioneer species start), S (Seral stages are intermediate), C (Climax is the stable end-state).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses 'Primary Productivity' (rate of biomass production) with 'Standing Crop' (total biomass at a given time). Remember: Productivity is a rate (energy/area/time).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Ecological Resilience' to describe the capacity of an ecosystem to absorb disturbance and reorganize while undergoing change.

keyTakeaways: Energy flows unidirectionally; nutrients cycle globally.
Succession is a predictable process driven by species interaction and environmental modification.
Ecosystem stability is directly proportional to biodiversity and functional redundancy.
